title: One slow server takes everyone down
summary: Round robin keeps feeding a server that slowed down; least-outstanding routing and health checks route around it.

takeaway.summary: Send each request to the server with the fewest in progress, and take a server that fails its health checks out of rotation until it passes again.
takeaway.timeComplexity: One comparison of in-progress counts per request
takeaway.spaceComplexity: One in-progress count and one health state per server
whenToUse: Servers whose speed can change: a noisy neighbor, a failing disk, a long garbage-collection pause
Any pool where one bad member shouldn't slow everyone

scenes.narration: Two app servers with 4 workers each sit behind a load balancer, which takes turns: one request to each. At 40 requests a second, both have room to spare. Then, 3 seconds in, server 2's disk slows down and its work takes 6 times longer.
scenes.caption: Two servers behind a round-robin balancer, both comfortable

scenes.narration: Follow two requests. R139 went to server 1. R140 arrives next, and round robin sends it to server 2 because it's server 2's turn. It doesn't look at how busy either server is.
scenes.caption: R140 arrives: round robin sends it to Server 2, whose turn it is

scenes.narration: Server 2 already has a queue, so R140 waits behind 5 requests. When it was routed, server 1 had 1 request in progress and 3 free workers. That breaks rule 1: never send a request to a full server while another has room.
scenes.caption: R140 waits behind 5 on Server 2 while Server 1 has 3 free workers

scenes.narration: R140 times out after a second. Over those 3 seconds, 41 requests timed out and 46 percent were slower than half a second or timed out, while server 1 stayed only about a third busy. These latencies are illustrative.
scenes.caption: 3 to 6 seconds: p99 hits the 1-second timeout, 46% of requests affected

scenes.narration: Two changes. Least-outstanding routing sends each request to the server with the fewest in progress: with equal servers, that one has a free worker whenever either does. Health checks take a server that can't answer out of rotation.
scenes.caption: Send work where there's room, and stop sending it where it can't finish

elements.reason: with equal servers, the emptiest one has room if anyone does
elements.label: where to send

scenes.narration: Replay the same slowdown with the fix. When R140 arrives, server 1 has 2 requests in progress and server 2 has 4, so least outstanding sends it to server 1, which finishes it in about 100 milliseconds.
scenes.caption: Same incident: least outstanding sends R140 to Server 1 instead

scenes.narration: Every second the balancer checks each server. Server 2 misses the 200-millisecond deadline twice in a row, so the balancer marks it unhealthy and stops sending it requests.
scenes.caption: Server 2 fails 2 health checks in a row: marked unhealthy

scenes.narration: With server 2 out of rotation, server 1 handles everything. Over those 3 seconds p99 is 177 milliseconds, nothing times out, and no request waited while a server had room.
scenes.caption: 6 to 9 seconds: Server 1 alone, p99 177 ms, no timeouts

scenes.narration: At 9 seconds server 2 is back to normal speed. It passes 2 health checks in a row, and the balancer marks it healthy and starts sending it requests again, with no one stepping in.
scenes.caption: Server 2 recovers, passes 2 checks, and gets requests again

scenes.narration: Checked over seeds 1 to 20 and four slowdowns, 3, 5, and 8 times slower and hanging, at 40 requests a second with both servers at 4 workers: round robin broke rule 1 in all 80 runs, the fix in none. The guarantee needs servers with the same number of workers. Route by load, and check health.
scenes.caption: Rule 1, seeds 1–20 × 4 slowdowns, both servers at 4 workers: fix 0 of 80
